title: Report MJPEG USB-camera modes as a compressed codec
problem: Linux device enumeration converts every V4L2 FourCC only to AVPixelFormat. MJPG is compressed and has no AVPixelFormat, so common high-resolution USB-camera modes surface as NONE with no usable format identity.
reproduce: At the pinned revision, v4l2FormatToAV handles raw FourCC values only. V4L2_PIX_FMT_MJPEG falls through to AV_PIX_FMT_NONE, matching the reporter’s null avGetPixFmtName output.
acceptance: MJPG and JPEG capture modes expose AV_CODEC_ID_MJPEG while retaining AV_PIX_FMT_NONE until decode; raw modes expose AV_CODEC_ID_RAWVIDEO plus their existing pixel format; codecId reaches both native APIs and the public TypeScript DeviceMode.
repair: Represent capture identity with both pixelFormat and codecId, map Linux MJPG/JPEG to the MJPEG codec, and carry the codec through synchronous, asynchronous, and TypeScript device-mode APIs.

verification.limitations: BCL proves the malformed baseline mapping and complete candidate API path. TypeScript library, tests and examples compile; the Linux translation unit compiles in Ubuntu 24.04. Full native linking needs the project’s prebuilt custom FFmpeg tree, and physical enumeration needs the reporter’s MJPG camera.
verification.ownerCheck: Run DeviceAPI.modes on the same /dev/video20 camera and confirm MJPG resolutions return codecId AV_CODEC_ID_MJPEG; avGetCodecName(mode.codecId) should return mjpeg while YUYV modes keep their existing pixelFormat.

selection.reason: A fresh USB-camera owner supplied exact V4L2 and NodeAV output at the current beta; no competing PR exists, and the missing compressed-format identity is deterministic in the pinned Linux mapping.

publish.commitMessage: fix: report MJPEG device modes as a codec

negative.outputIncludes: DeviceMode must expose compressed capture codecs
